evidence.positive: Against the running app (mayo-mayo tenant, http://localhost:56363) I confirmed the Risk column is imported and that it narrows the walk. DB: "mayo-mayo".antibiotic_pathways for p-pancreatectomy holds exactly two rows, position 0 risk=LOW and position 1 risk=HIGH, matching the two Risk-column rows in mayo/procedures/antibiotic-pathways.csv. I then created two Mayo cases carrying p-pancreatectomy via POST /api/admin/patients/ and /operations/create, and set the procedure's rated risk in operation_procedure_types.calculated_attributes ('{"risk":"low"}' on case 98634, '{"risk":"high"}' on case 87353). GET /api/admin/patients/{pmrn}/operations/{caseId}/antibiotic-candidates (which drops the cache and re-runs ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.resolve) returned for the high-risk case: procedureRisk=HIGH, recommended=[CEFTRIAXONE, METRONIDAZOLE], pathway pos=1 risk=HIGH appliesToCase=true status RECOMMENDED. For the low-risk case: procedureRisk=LOW, recommended=[CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE], pathway pos=0 risk=LOW appliesToCase=true. Third bullet confirmed on a third case (37125) whose calculated_attributes were '{}' (never rated): procedureRisk=null, yet pathway pos=0 risk=LOW appliesToCase=true and recommended=[CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE] - an absent rating reads as LOW. An unreadable token ('{"risk":"medium"}') behaved the same way. Bullet 1's 'no risk applies at every risk' was exercised by temporarily clearing the HIGH row's risk: with risk=null that pathway showed appliesToCase=true against both the LOW and the HIGH case. The same walk was also driven through the real rule-engine path (POST /api/admin/events/category-event, INDUCTION_START on case 87353), which logged 'Finished ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.resolve - 74.35 ms' for operation 01a04a0a-d691-75bc-9311-9b264a300279.
evidence.negative: The pathway written for the other risk is not merely outranked - it is never walked. On the high-risk case 87353 the LOW pathway (CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE) came back appliesToCase=false with both of its steps NOT_SELECTED, and CEFAZOLIN appeared nowhere in 'recommended' and nowhere in 'contraindicated' (which was empty) - it neither survived nor died. Symmetrically, on the low-risk case 98634 the HIGH pathway (CEFTRIAXONE AND METRONIDAZOLE) came back appliesToCase=false, all steps NOT_SELECTED, and CEFTRIAXONE was absent from 'recommended' and from 'contraindicated'. In both directions the case's single recommendation was the one step from the one in-scope pathway.
evidence.red_check: Two data flips, both reverted and both re-verified. (1) I set both p-pancreatectomy pathway rows to risk='HIGH' in "mayo-mayo".antibiotic_pathways and re-ran the low-risk case 98634: outcome flipped from RECOMMENDED to NOT_CONFIGURED, recommended=[], both pathways appliesToCase=false, and the app logged 'Operation 01a04a09-9913-7784-b859-471a4154fec8 matched no antibiotic pathway for p-pancreatectomy: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity none' - proving the risk filter really removes pathways before the walk rather than the walk merely preferring one. (2) I cleared the HIGH row's risk to NULL (the pre-fix world where the two pancreatectomy protocols compete as tiers of one ladder) and re-ran the same low-risk case: the CEFTRIAXONE pathway went appliesToCase=true and 'recommended' became two co-equal step-1 options, [CEFAZOLIN, METRONIDAZOLE] and [CEFTRIAXONE, METRONIDAZOLE] - the exact absence assertion above going red. I also flipped the input file: uploading a Mayo antibiotic-pathways.csv with Risk='medium' on the high-risk row via POST /api/admin/config-imports/antibiotic-pathways/upload logged 'row 71: Skipping pathway with unrecognized Risk: medium' followed by 'Dropping the risk-scoped pathways for p-pancreatectomy: only [LOW] configured, so any other risk would resolve to no guidance at all', leaving zero pancreatectomy pathway rows and the case NOT_CONFIGURED. I then re-uploaded the shipped CSV (recordCountAfter back to 463), confirmed the rows are again position 0=LOW / position 1=HIGH, and re-ran all three cases - LOW gets cefazolin, HIGH gets ceftriaxone, unrated gets cefazolin, exactly as before the flips.

red_check_signature: matched no antibiotic pathway for p-pancreatectomy: 2 configured, procedure risk LOW case acuity none
caveats: The rated risk was written straight into operation_procedure_types.calculated_attributes rather than produced by ProcedureRiskService, because applyProcedureRisk only runs inside OperationService.startOperation, which is reachable only through POST /api/app-launch and that call needs the real Mayo Epic FHIR endpoint. The rating logic is a different ticket; what was validated is that the walk reads that value and scopes on it.
Only the Mayo tenant ships risk-scoped pathways today (p-pancreatectomy, low/high); demo and mgb have an empty Risk column throughout, so no other tenant's configuration exercises this path.

The walk was driven through the admin antibiotic-candidates endpoint, which calls the same ProcedureAntibioticCandidateService.resolve the rule engine uses; a category event confirmed resolve runs in the rule-engine path too, but the antibiotic alert text a clinician would actually see was not rendered.

The in-app debugger UI that renders risk and appliesToCase was not opened in a browser - the DTO feeding it was read over the API instead. That UI belongs to the debugger tickets rather than to this one.
Acuity scoping was not re-validated here; all cases carried a null acuity, so only the risk half of AntibioticPathway.appliesTo was exercised.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage is already strong and specific: AntibioticPathwayResolutionSpecTest has riskScopedPathwayAppliesOnlyAtThatRisk, unscopedPathwayAppliesAtEveryRisk, caseWithoutRiskReadsAsLowRisk, acuityAndRiskAreBothRequired, cache_aRiskChangeDropsEveryReadersAnswerForTheCase and theExplanationListsPathwaysScopedToTheOtherRisk; AntibioticPathwayCSVImporterTest covers the Risk column and the unrecognized-token reject. The gap is the shipped Mayo configuration itself - nothing asserts that mayo/procedures/antibiotic-pathways.csv actually yields the low/high pancreatectomy pair, so a typo in the Risk cell would silently trip dropIncompleteRiskScopes and take pancreatectomy guidance to zero pathways with only a WARN, which is what the flip reproduced here.
proposed_tests: Extend MayoProcedureConfigImportIntegrationTest to assert the shipped mayo antibiotic-pathways.csv imports exactly two p-pancreatectomy pathways, one risk=LOW with notation 'CEFAZOLIN AND METRONIDAZOLE -> LEVOFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE' and one risk=HIGH with 'CEFTRIAXONE AND METRONIDAZOLE -> LEVOFLOXACIN AND METRONIDAZOLE'.

Add an importer test that a procedure whose only risk-scoped rows cover a single risk ends with no pathways at all for that procedure, locking in dropIncompleteRiskScopes as a guard rather than an accident.

Add a resolution spec case asserting that a pathway scoped to the other risk is absent from both preferred and contraindicated, so 'neither survives nor dies' is pinned rather than inferred from the recommendation alone.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A Mayo pancreatectomy case rated high risk resolved to ceftriaxone plus metronidazole, a case rated low risk resolved to cefazolin plus metronidazole, and a case with no rating at all resolved to the low-risk pathway.
Negative: The pathway written for the other risk was reported as out of scope and appeared in neither the recommended nor the contraindicated list, so it neither survived nor died.
Red check: Clearing the risk on the high-risk pathway row put ceftriaxone back in front of a low-risk case, and scoping both rows to high left the low-risk case with no pathway at all and a matching log line; both flips were reverted and the original behaviour re-confirmed.

Automation: Unit coverage of the scoping rules is already thorough, so the proposal is to pin the shipped Mayo configuration and the incomplete-risk-scope guard.
